knowledge_point.title: Identifying an Invertible Function From Its Graph

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124472/assets/280f8c4e9774092abf50d5579f193963a078c8f77712c6db3a8ca65ce9bc697e.png)

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?

Each graph shows its entire domain; an open circle excludes its endpoint.

Select all that apply.

Graph positions: **I.** upper left; **II.** upper right; **III.** lower left; **IV.** lower right.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124472/assets/889919bb2ab525afba1f0056875c761524fb0ad3fa4db8b609a00c0592a70625.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graph IV, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, this graph shows a one-to-one function. As a result, this function is invertible.

- For graphs I, II, III, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.
